title: Cross-modal Fusion Transformer for Integrating Retrieved Knowledge into Video Caption Generation

problem.claim: Long-form video captioning is challenging for untrimmed videos because visual evidence can be incomplete and crucial semantics may be implied rather than directly observable.

gap.claim: Existing hierarchical captioning models rely primarily on the visual stream, while existing knowledge integrations are often shallow and insensitive to retrieval reliability.

contributions.claim: A video-aware knowledge fusion approach integrates retrieved knowledge at the feature level before generation.
The approach combines confidence- and visual-context-based contextual gating with a cross-modal fusion transformer over video and gated-knowledge query tokens.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The full model improves CIDEr by up to 11.1% on YouCook2 and by 4.2% and 5.8% on Ego4D-HCap segment descriptions and video summaries, respectively, compared with a strong baseline.
The paper reports that integrating knowledge at the feature stage improves semantic coverage when generating captions for long-form videos.

narrative_sequence.summary: Long-form video captioning supports indexing, accessibility, and downstream video analytics.
Untrimmed videos contain incomplete visual evidence and implied semantics.
Existing visual and knowledge-integration approaches can omit entities or relations and are vulnerable to noisy retrieval evidence.
The proposed method performs feature-level knowledge fusion using retrieval-aware gating and cross-modal transformer refinement.
The full model reports CIDEr improvements over a strong baseline on YouCook2 and Ego4D-HCap.

source_observation.claim: Retrieved knowledge is integrated before generation and modulated using retrieval confidence and pooled visual context.

interpretation.claim: Early, reliability-aware cross-modal fusion may help compensate for incomplete visual evidence while limiting the influence of noisy retrievals.

application.claim: For multimodal generation with uncertain external evidence, fuse retrieved information at the feature level and condition its strength on reliability signals.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the approach remains effective when retrieval confidence is poorly calibrated or retrieval quality differs substantially across domains.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the retrieval sources, confidence-signal construction, or training procedure.
The abstract does not provide ablations, statistical significance, or results beyond the reported CIDEr improvements.
